A_target.statement:
Let $X$ be a [[Definition:Connected Topological Space|connected]] [[Definition:Topological Space|topological space]] and $f: X \to Y$ [[Definition:Continuous Mapping (Topology)|continuous]].
Then $\map f X$ is connected.

B_source.statement: A topological space $Z$ is connected {{iff}} every continuous mapping $g: Z \to \set {0, 1}$, where $\set {0, 1}$ is [[Definition:Discrete Topology|discrete]], is [[Definition:Constant Mapping|constant]].

substitutions.the test map g: a two-valued continuous map on f(X)

derived.composing with f: a two-valued continuous map on X

object_map.reformulation: Test connectedness of the image by composing two-valued maps with f.

validity_conditions: The corestriction of f to its image is continuous.
Surjectivity onto the image is what transfers constancy back from X.
proof_plan: Then $g \circ f: X \to \set {0, 1}$ is continuous, as a composite of continuous mappings.
As $X$ is connected, $g \circ f$ is constant by the source result.
